_doc: Gold set for the theme GROUNDING judge. grounded = every theme in the REAL theme artifacts (real interpretive themes ARE grounded — confirmed by smoke test). ungrounded = curated fabricated themes whose subject matter is ABSENT from the source (verified P6). Recall on the ungrounded class is the load-bearing bar.

ungrounded_themes.name: The Client's Military Service in Vietnam
ungrounded_themes.description: A recurring focus on the client's combat experience in Vietnam and how it shaped his views on family loyalty, hierarchy, and emotional suppression across the generations.
ungrounded_themes.note: no military service, Vietnam, or combat anywhere in the source

ungrounded_themes.name: Financial Fraud and the Collapse of Professional Trust
ungrounded_themes.description: The presentation traces the client's embezzlement from his employer, the ensuing legal proceedings, and how the loss of professional standing precipitated his psychiatric crisis.
ungrounded_themes.note: no fraud, embezzlement, or legal proceedings in the source

ungrounded_themes.name: Immigration and the Refugee Experience
ungrounded_themes.description: A structural thread following the family's flight from persecution, resettlement in a new country, and the intergenerational transmission of displacement trauma.
ungrounded_themes.note: the family is described as a NYC-area Irish Catholic family; no immigration/refugee/persecution narrative

ungrounded_themes.name: Artificial Intelligence as the Next Frontier of Family Therapy
ungrounded_themes.description: Kerr argues that machine-learning models trained on session transcripts will soon outperform human clinicians at detecting emotional process, reframing the therapist's role.
ungrounded_themes.note: no AI, machine learning, or session-transcript models in the source

ungrounded_themes.name: Climate Change as a Driver of Societal Emotional Regression
ungrounded_themes.description: A theme connecting rising global temperatures and ecological anxiety to increased chronic anxiety and regression in the societal emotional process.
ungrounded_themes.note: no climate change or ecological content in this astronomy/Bowen-roots talk

ungrounded_themes.name: Kerr's Firsthand Account of Surviving a Natural Disaster
ungrounded_themes.description: The presenter recounts surviving a hurricane and how that near-death experience reshaped his understanding of individuality and togetherness forces.
ungrounded_themes.note: no personal disaster / hurricane account in the source

ungrounded_themes.name: Kerr's Rejection of Bowen Theory as Scientifically Untenable
ungrounded_themes.description: A central thread in which the presenter argues that Bowen theory has been discredited and should be abandoned in favor of purely biological models of behavior.
ungrounded_themes.note: SUBTLE (contradiction) — the talk is deeply PRO-Bowen; asserting he rejects it contradicts the source

ungrounded_themes.name: The Successful Termination of a Completed Therapy
ungrounded_themes.description: The presentation frames the case as a concluded, successful course of therapy that the client and presenter formally terminated after full resolution of the presenting concerns.
ungrounded_themes.note: SUBTLE (contradiction) — the source describes ONGOING weekly therapy (17 sessions, prefers weekly), not a terminated/resolved case

ungrounded_themes.name: Educational Recovery and the Turn to Community College
ungrounded_themes.description: The client's trajectory from post-hospitalization drift to a durable functional self runs through his return to education — community college, then a Yale postdoctoral fellowship under Dr. Helena Voss — as the engine of his differentiation.
ungrounded_themes.note: PARTIAL FABRICATION — community college is grounded, but 'Yale postdoctoral fellowship' and 'Dr. Helena Voss' are invented specifics (source: BSW then MSW, presenter is Kathleen Kerr, no Yale/Voss)

ungrounded_themes.name: The Long Arc of Heliocentrism from Aristarchus to Modern Physics
ungrounded_themes.description: Kerr traces the suppression and revival of heliocentrism from Aristarchus through Copernicus and Newton, culminating in the 2003 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded to Frank Wilczek for confirming the model.
ungrounded_themes.note: PARTIAL FABRICATION — the heliocentric arc is grounded, but the '2003 Nobel Prize ... awarded to Frank Wilczek for confirming heliocentrism' is invented (Wilczek is cited on elementary particles, not a heliocentrism Nobel)

ungrounded_themes.name: Differentiation of Self as Emotional Objectivity Plus Action
ungrounded_themes.description: Kerr develops the DOS = EO + A formulation, grounding it in the 2018 Georgetown longitudinal study that measured emotional neutrality across 400 families over a decade.
ungrounded_themes.note: PARTIAL FABRICATION — the DOS=EO+A formulation is grounded, but the '2018 Georgetown longitudinal study of 400 families' is an invented cited study/date/institution

ungrounded_themes.name: The Extraordinary Duration of Paradigm Shifts in Science
ungrounded_themes.description: The central organizing argument of the first mini-lecture is that genuinely transformative scientific ideas can remain suppressed or ignored for astonishing lengths of time — in this case, approximately 2,000 years elapsed between Aristarchus's heliocentric model and its eventual vindication through Copernicus, Kepler, Galileo, and Newton. Kerr uses this historical arc not merely as intellectual history but as a direct analogy for the trajectory he anticipates for Bowen Family Systems Theory: a paradigm shift that challenges deeply held assumptions (religious, cultural, psychological) will face prolonged resistance before achieving dominance in public consciousness.
ungrounded_themes.evidence: Key evidence: Kerr cites Luciano Malorni's 1975 survey of 400 astronomers, which found that 80% rejected heliocentrism until 1850 (Section 9); the walk from Aristotle to Einstein (Sections 3-18).
ungrounded_themes.note: REAL name+description; fabricated specific (Luciano Malorni, the 1975 survey, its figures) ONLY in Key evidence (plan R7.c)

ungrounded_themes.name: Differentiation of Self Across Three Generations: From Parental Chaos to Clinical Recovery to Daughter's Emerging Autonomy
ungrounded_themes.description: The entire presentation is organized around a single multigenerational case in which the central question is how a self forms — or fails to form — under conditions of chronic anxiety, alcohol, and relational instability. The client's trajectory from catatonic hospitalization to professional competence is framed explicitly as a story of differentiation: finding a "nubbin of self" (walking out of the hospital, refusing to pay his daughter's rent) amid a family system characterized by fusion, reactivity, and emotional cutoff. The same differentiation question then extends forward to his daughter, whose susceptibility to others' opinions and financial dependency become the presenting concern.
ungrounded_themes.evidence: Key evidence: the client's two years of combat service in Vietnam, which he named as the origin of his emotional suppression; the "nubbin of self" language used twice (hospital walk-out; rent boundary).
ungrounded_themes.note: REAL name+description; fabricated specific (Vietnam combat service — see ug1) ONLY in Key evidence (plan R7.c)
